issues.description: The template class QFTNQubit defines the forward QFT method with the name `_qft_circuit_n_qubits` (leading underscore), while the solution implements it as `qft_circuit_n_qubits` (no leading underscore) and the problem statement refers to implementing QFT for arbitrary number of qubits. This name/signature mismatch is a structural inconsistency in the API students are expected to implement and will cause confusion or test failures (students following the template will implement/override the wrong method name).
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the forward QFT method in the template from `_qft_circuit_n_qubits` to `qft_circuit_n_qubits` (remove the leading underscore) so the template, solution, and problem statement use the same method name/signature. Alternatively, adjust the problem statement/tests to expect the underscored name, but the simpler fix is to align the template method name with the intended public API `qft_circuit_n_qubits`.

issues.description: The template defines the QFT function for N qubits with a leading underscore in its name (_qft_circuit_n_qubits), whereas the solution and the problem statement refer to the same conceptual routine as qft_circuit_n_qubits. This inconsistent identifier for the same core concept (the QFT for n qubits) creates a mapping burden: students following the problem statement or comparing to the solution may not find the expected method name in the template, and automated tests referencing qft_circuit_n_qubits may fail or confuse learners.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method _qft_circuit_n_qubits to qft_circuit_n_qubits (remove the leading underscore) so the template, problem statement, and solution use the exact same identifier for the QFT-for-n-qubits routine. Ensure any references/tests use the unified name.
